title: Microsoft Purview DLP: set policy tips and email notifications separately for SharePoint and OneDrive rules (Worldwide)
summary: The roadmap facts, licensing and PowerShell controls are supported. The portal routes need minor completion, and Microsoft Learn gives conflicting guidance about email notifications when existing files change; the briefing should acknowledge that conflict.

claims.claim: The printed Microsoft Purview portal route reaches the documented policy-tip option while creating a rule.
claims.quote: Set the User Notifications toggle to On. Select Notify users in Office 365 services with a policy tip and then select Notify the user who sent, shared, or last modified the content.
claims.fix: In front matter and the rendered table, complete the route as 'Data loss prevention > Policies > Create policy > Enterprise applications & devices > Categories > Custom > Regulations > Custom > Assign admin units > Full directory > Choose where to apply the policy > SharePoint sites > OneDrive accounts > Define policy settings > Create or customize advanced DLP rules > Customize advanced DLP rules > Create rule > User Notifications > Notify users in Office 365 services with a policy tip'. Retain the note that this route documents the policy-tip option rather than all four combinations, and add 'Set User Notifications to On.' The omitted items are headings, scope selections and an already-selected advanced-rule option, not a wrong route. Source: https://learn.microsoft.com/purview/dlp-create-policy-spo-odb-external.

claims.claim: Set-DlpComplianceRule -Identity <rule> -NotifyUserType Email,PolicyTip sets the rule notification type to both.
claims.quote: The Identity parameter specifies the DLP rule that you want to modify. ... The NotifyUserType parameter specifies the type of notification that's used for the rule. Valid values are: NotSet; Email; PolicyTip; Email,PolicyTip

claims.claim: The printed Microsoft Purview portal route reaches Allow override from M365 services under User overrides.
claims.quote: Under User overrides, make sure that Allow override from M365 services is NOT selected.
claims.fix: In front matter and the rendered table, complete the route as 'Data loss prevention > Policies > Create policy > Enterprise applications & devices > Categories > Custom > Regulations > Custom > Assign admin units > Full directory > Choose where to apply the policy > SharePoint sites > OneDrive accounts > Define policy settings > Create or customize advanced DLP rules > Customize advanced DLP rules > Create rule > User overrides > Allow override from M365 services'. The omitted items are headings, scope selections and an already-selected advanced-rule option, not a wrong route. Source: https://learn.microsoft.com/purview/dlp-create-policy-spo-odb-external.
